execution: Independent scratch patch per feature and variant; deterministic protocol responder/replay only; no provider latency or semantic-quality claim
common_rules: Use the runtime's formal frozen baseline, not a mutable calibration tree.
Apply each feature independently to A/B/C with identical externally visible requirements.
Count actual changed operational Rust modules, including newly added operational modules when used; retain exact diffs, implementation time, repair revisions and acceptance logs.
Do not split or merge modules to force a score difference. Ties are valid.
Retain existing whole-source revision/revocation and source-backed completion guards.
Original read model prompts and actual model outputs are not replaced by oracle content in measured candidates. Offline semantic responses are explicitly test doubles.
Keep failed patches/acceptance attempts and exclude all QA04 replay timing from actual model QA01/QA03.

tasks.name: Query provenance of an actually delivered answer
tasks.input_contract: Explicit UI action identifying a previously delivered response/goal ID. It does not require a new natural-language semantic classifier.
expected: A successful actual complete callback registers queryable original source identity, source revision and inclusive extent from its delivered fact provenance.
Return source metadata and current usability separately from historical delivered provenance; do not claim an obsolete revision is current.
Unpresented initial proposals, rejected answers and exhausted repairs are never registered as delivered answers.
Unknown response ID returns NO_MATCH. Repeated lookup is read-only and leaves the answer and task unchanged.
Use the existing outputs/delivery lifecycle if sufficient; a one-module tie across ABC is acceptable.

tasks.name: Withdraw a proper subrange of an evidence source
tasks.input_contract: Trusted user authority event: source_id, current source revision, inclusive one-based start/end line, new access epoch. This is a permission event, never a referent/semantic oracle hint.
expected: Block newly requested original reads and actual model/adoption use that overlap the withdrawn range, including old spans from before the authority change.

Keep nonoverlapping source ranges available. A retained raw view can preserve or split unaffected raw passages; a derived assertion spanning a withdrawn range must be blocked rather than host-reinterpreted.
Filter source-dependent recent delivered facts before later model transmission without resurrecting withdrawn text through a whole-answer string.
C producer reads only remaining authorized segments; current valid records survive and affected records cannot be consumed or republished from old state.
B request-local evidence and any active returned bundle must obey the same common span authority.
Do not represent past external disclosure as recalled; this feature blocks new use after the event.

tasks.name: Apply a section-specific incremental Agent artifact update
tasks.input_contract: A real received typed artifact update with task_id, artifact_id, section_id, base_revision, new_revision, replacement text and source provenance; no external action is replayed.
expected: Bind an accepted section update to its existing Task/artifact and display the changed section with actual delivery history.
Leave other artifact sections, unrelated tasks/delegations and their delivery state unchanged.
Reject stale base_revision, duplicate new_revision, unknown artifact/section and task mismatch; retain rejected evidence.
Queued text/audio references to the changed section resolve to the new accepted section revision. Voice remains OFF; do not claim TTS performance.
Expose the updated public artifact as source-backed evidence for later handoff: current source vector/manifest and any B work-record dependencies must no longer admit the obsolete section.
Do not rebuild or silently alter unrelated sections or send real external actions.

tasks.name: Withdraw part of a handoff source
tasks.input_contract: Trusted source-range authority event with revision and access epoch, as for DP01. Same source remains partially usable.
expected: Manifest reports remaining usable segments and receiver range reads deny overlap with the withdrawn part while serving allowed ranges.
Capsule references/passages and B work-record spans from the old access epoch cannot be newly admitted if they overlap the withdrawn part.
Retain valid unaffected blocks/references and avoid whole-source denial merely because one range was withdrawn.
B future producer excludes withdrawn segments and does not reintroduce old text through previous_record.
All A/B/C receivers share the same access checks and do not gain broader ranges through a valid old manifest.
Record actual denied range receipts; whole-source revision/revocation still rejects stale and revoked spans.
